title: Asia Markets Mixed Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
summary: Gotrade News - Asian stock markets traded mixed on Wednesday, September 23, as investors held back ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump
body_markdown:
Chip stocks drove much of that move. The AP reported that[Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) jumped 9.9% to a market value of $1 trillion and[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) added 2.3%, a rebound covered in[the AI chip rally that reignited this week](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/ai-chip-rally-reignites-tonight/) . US stock futures were largely unchanged on Wednesday, and Brent crude slipped 0.72% to around $99 per barrel, per[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/asia-stocks-struggle-for-direction-ahead-of-trumpxi-meeting-china-shares-down-4912042) .


## Trade Truce Expiry Puts Chips and Soybeans in Focus


The stakes are tied to a deadline. Per[Investing.com's summit outlook](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/trumpxi-summit-outlook-watch-these-chinese-stocks-and-sectors-93CH-4908238) , the current trade truce, which caps duties at about 20%, expires in early November, making this summit "the last clean window for a deal before tariff brinkmanship restarts." Goldman Sachs' base case, as cited in the same report, is a "delay" scenario in which the truce is quietly extended rather than a comprehensive deal.


The report names semiconductor export controls on AI chips, rare earths access, EV battery localization, and US crude and soybean purchase pledges as the signals to watch. Soybean purchase volumes are relevant for agricultural processors such as[Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/adm/) , while any change in chip licensing language would matter for Nvidia and AMD. For more on the rate backdrop, see the[weekly market outlook on the Fed hike and 5% yields](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/weekly-economic-outlook-2026-09-21/) .


Investors on[Gotrade](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/) following US stocks exposed to China may see headline-driven swings through Thursday's meeting, as outcomes remain uncertain and no deal terms have been announced.
